label: sequence started with c (input steps 3+ through <DEL>)
explanation: Fires on every original-phase input from step 3 onward, and on the <DEL> step, in sequences whose first original token is c (first_tok=c lift 24x, 97% of activation mass). Never fires at t=0-2 and almost never in the copy phase. The <DEL> step is where it outputs c (out_tok=c). The activation ramps up after step 3, peaks around steps 4-6, and drops a little at <DEL>. All of the top examples begin with c c, so a second c seems to make it larger. Weak sub-threshold activity in sequences where c is the second token (for example w c ...) accounts for most of the missed low-quartile activations. Which token is input at the current step barely matters.

issues: The claims hold up on the test split. The predicate gets precision 0.992, recall 0.81, F1 0.892 and mass recall 0.967, matching the reported scores. There are only 597 false positives, mostly at t=3 in sequences like c x c ..., where the feature is late to switch on.
The claim that it barely fires in the copy phase is confirmed: phase==2 holds 0.04% of activation mass on test (197 active steps on dev). It is never active at t=0-2.

The magnitude profile is confirmed. Steps 4-6 have precision 1.0 and hold 64% of mass, with 85% coverage of the top activation quartile. t=3 is mostly in the lower two quartiles. The <DEL> step (precision 0.998, 20% of mass) sits in the middle quartiles, so it does drop a little.

The 'second c makes it larger' claim is only weakly supported. Sequences starting c c make up 3.3% of the predicate's steps but 8% of top-quartile coverage, so the boost is modest, and the explanation already hedges it.

The misses form one systematic class, but it is low-magnitude: 17.6k missed steps, which is 19% of active steps but only 3.3% of mass. Of that 19%, 14.3 points come from sequences where c is the 2nd or 3rd original token (precision 5.6%, 2.9% of mass). The explanation already notes this weak activity.
Adding the second-position-c case lowers F1 to 0.79 (precision 0.67), so the original predicate is the best one tested. The label matches the predicate.
